question:
In the pattern below, the cat moves clockwise through the four squares and the mouse moves counterclockwise through the eight exterior segments of the four squares.

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

If the pattern is continued, where would the cat and mouse be after the \(247\)th move?
solution:
The cat returns to the same square every four moves, and the mouse returns to the same exterior segment every eight moves. Thus eight moves return both animals to their previous positions: the cat completes two circuits while the mouse completes one.

Since
\[
247=30\cdot8+7,
\]
move \(247\) has the same positions as move \(7\).

The cat's position at move \(7\) matches its position at move \(3\), four moves earlier, so it is in the lower-right square. At move \(5\), the mouse is on the left half of the top exterior edge. Continuing counterclockwise puts it on the upper half of the left edge at move \(6\), then the lower half of the left edge at move \(7\). These positions give choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
